ANSWER: The enforcement happens in two files:

**`pkg/okf/provenance.go` — `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification` (line 26)**
This function is the guard. It receives the acting `actor` string and the concept being saved. If the actor is *not* a human identity (checked via `IsHumanIdentity`), it iterates over all `Verified` entries on the concept. For any entry whose `By` field names a human and that wasn't already present in the on-disk file (`recordedVerifications`), it returns an error:
```
"actor %q cannot add human verification %q"
```
This blocks any non-human actor (e.g. `agent/mcp-server`) from injecting a new human verification entry.

**`pkg/okf/mutate.go` — the concept-save path (line 494)**
This is the call site. During a `SaveConcept` operation, after resolving the actor (defaulting to `"agent/okf-tool"` if blank), it calls `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification(fullPath, c, actor, opts.IsNew)` and returns immediately on error. This is the only gate before the concept is written to disk.

Supporting helpers also in `pkg/okf/provenance.go`:
- **`IsHumanIdentity`** (line 12) — determines whether the actor string represents a human (vs. agent/machine).
- **`recordedVerifications`** (line 43) — reads the existing on-disk concept to get the set of verifications already recorded, so only *newly added* human verifications are blocked (preserving pre-existing ones).

CONFIDENCE: high
